structured_output.world_model: W6: time ≈ 0.1 s + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is pixel-proportional compute plus a bandwidth-bound part. The tip, E061, is 5.02 s and 0.7534 on seeds 0–2. Its population mean is about 0.7530–0.7535. The ±0.2 pp rebuild noise on seeds 0–2 dominates single-run reads. Time-neutral changes (LR table, anneal end, optimizer constants) give a time of 5.0 ± 0.06. Accuracy changes from small hyperparameter tweaks are mostly within ±0.15 pp. E062 shows the recipe is sensitive to the optimizer's per-step quality, so Muon lr and momentum changes can move accuracy by more than the dial. Muon momentum 0.8 probably hurts, because batch 2000 is already large and 225 steps is short. A Muon lr of ×1.5 is a coin flip near zero. Moving the anneal end to 80% is a mild slow-decay change, probably within noise. Moving the detach to 80% adds about 0.09 s for a tiny gain. The Muon systems merge saves about 0.03–0.08 s. The diagnostic I109 has no time or accuracy metric of its own; the run behaves like the tip.

forecasts.reason: Time-neutral anneal-end shift; the effect is likely under the noise of 3 seeds.
Costs about 0.09 s for a gain of 0.05–0.1 pp, which is roughly at the dial's rate.
Muon lr ×1.5 gave a small positive read at 3 seeds before; I expect a gain near zero.
Merging the Muon calls probably saves 0.03–0.08 s, with accuracy unchanged within rebuild noise.
Higher momentum with a large batch and few steps more likely hurts, though the 0.6 value was never tuned.
Diagnostic with no recipe change; I expect train top-1 well below saturation, around 80–90% (under-fitting).

cruxes: Is the rebuild SD of a 20-seed mean about 0.05 pp or larger? That sets whether any sub-0.1 pp booster is detectable.
Does the Muon lr or momentum optimum shift for this 225-step regime? E062 says optimizer quality dominates.
How much of the Muon optimizer section is host or launch overhead rather than GPU time? That sets the systems saving, which is up to about 0.05 s.
